videos.title: What to Do the Moment You Open Your Eyes
videos.description:
The first hour after you wake up is when your brain is easiest to shape.
Most of us give it away.
We grab our phone and start scrolling.
Then we wonder why the day already feels hard.

In this clip, Jay Shetty shares the simple morning routine he tried himself. Every step is backed by research on how your brain works. And none of them take much time.

Jay explains why the snooze button might be the worst thing you do all morning. He shares a strange alarm trick that uses your own voice and he talks about how 10 minutes of sunlight can help you sleep better tonight.

Learn why ending your shower with 90 seconds of cold water calms you down hours later. And learn the three questions Jay says to write by hand every morning.

videos.title: Breaking the Codependency Cycle | Dr. Anna Lembke
videos.description:
Dr. Anna Lembke, MD, is chief of the Addiction Medicine Dual Diagnosis Clinic at Stanford Medicine and a leading expert in how to overcome addictions of all kinds.

We discuss dopamine dynamics in the brain and how they impact risk-taking, mental obsession, and compulsive behaviors.

We also discuss the most common addiction of all—people’s addiction to control—how codependency is a common form of that and how prayer and spiritual practices can open up new neural pathways and help end unhealthy thought patterns and behaviors, including codependence.

Anna is the author of the Dopamine Nation and a new book “Radical Surrender” which gets into the seemingly paradoxical fact that when people give up trying to control certain thought patterns or behaviors they actually are able to access new strategies to do so. I’ve read the book and it’s amazing. Lots of science and actionable tools.

This new podcast released today we brought in your understanding of dopamine and addictive and compulsive behaviors, codependency and much more.

Please put any questions or comments you might have below.

Thank you for your interest in science!

@stanford.med @stanford
